body.statement:
Let \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\).  If the entries of \(P\) are real algebraic, then a terminating real-closed-field quantifier-elimination procedure applied to the principal-minor form of the finite lift returns exact semialgebraic descriptions of both coordinate projections of
\[
 \{(c,\Delta):c>0,\ (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_v(P)\}
\]
onto the positive slope-odds coordinate \(c\) and the APE coordinate \(\Delta\).  If, in addition, queried values \(c>0\) and \(\Delta\) are real algebraic, the same procedure decides whether \((\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_v(P)\).  If \(P\) and \(c>0\) are real algebraic and the fixed-\(c\) fiber is nonempty, then its finite endpoints \(L_c^v(P)\) and \(U_c^v(P)\) are real algebraic, are computed by terminating elimination, and their two separate endpoint-inclusion flags are decidable.  No cellwise-positivity premise is required.
body.justification: Principal minors and real-closed-field elimination give projection descriptions, membership decisions, and endpoint decisions under their separate algebraic-input premises.
body.gap: Endpoint algebraicity additionally requires algebraic fixed \(c\) and a nonempty fixed-slope fiber; no positive-cell premise is needed.
body.consumer: It supplies exact symbolic benchmarks without support or slope grids.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), write \(z_{\mathrm w}=(m,a,b)\) and \(z_+=(m,a,b,t)\), and let
\[
 \Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)
\]
be the conjunction of \(c>0\), the sixteen observed-cell equalities, the APE equality with value \(d\), and all matrix inequalities in \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}principal\text{-}minor\text{-}psd}\), each fixed-size matrix inequality is equivalent to the nonnegativity of its finitely many principal minors.  The coefficients of every polynomial \(A_{xz,yw}\) and \(N_c\) are integer polynomials in \(c\), and every entry of \(H_s\), \(K_s\), and \(R_s\) is affine in the lift variables.  Consequently \(\Phi_v\) is a first-order ordered-field formula with parameters equal to the entries of \(P\).  The logarithm does not occur in this formula: \(c\) is the algebraic slope-odds coordinate, and the structural slope is recovered afterward as \(\log c\).

For every \(P\in\Delta^{15}\), including boundary laws, \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\) gives
\[
 (\log c,d)\in\Theta_v(P)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v). \tag{1}
\]
If \(P,c,d\) are real algebraic, the right side of (1) is a sentence with real algebraic coefficients.  The terminating procedure in \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}elimination}\) converts it into an equivalent quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions.  Signs of real algebraic numbers are decidable, so this decides membership.  Weak inequalities retain all singular PSD faces.

When only \(P\) is fixed, the two coordinate projections are defined by
\[
 \mathcal C_v(P)=\{c:\exists d,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_v(P)=\{d:\exists c,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\}. \tag{2}
\]
The restriction \(c>0\) is included in \(\Phi_v\).  If the entries of \(P\) are real algebraic, eliminating the quantified variables in (2) terminates and yields exact finite Boolean combinations of polynomial sign conditions for both projections.  This conclusion concerns projection onto \(c\), not a semialgebraic projection onto \(\theta=\log c\).

Now fix algebraic \(P\) and algebraic \(c>0\), and suppose the fixed-\(c\) fiber is nonempty.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}slope\text{-}endpoints}\), both endpoints are finite.  A real number \(\ell\) is its lower endpoint exactly when
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Inf}_v(\ell)\;:\!\Longleftrightarrow{}&
 \bigl[\exists d,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall d,z_v\,\{\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\Rightarrow \ell\le d\}\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall\varepsilon\,\{\varepsilon>0\Rightarrow
 \exists d,z_v\,[\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\wedge d<\ell+\varepsilon]\}\bigr].
\end{aligned}\tag{3}
\]
Similarly, \(r\) is its upper endpoint exactly when
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Sup}_v(r)\;:\!\Longleftrightarrow{}&
 \bigl[\exists d,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall d,z_v\,\{\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\Rightarrow d\le r\}\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall\varepsilon\,\{\varepsilon>0\Rightarrow
 \exists d,z_v\,[\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\wedge r-\varepsilon<d]\}\bigr].
\end{aligned}\tag{4}
\]
Quantifier elimination applied to (3) and (4) gives semialgebraic descriptions, over the real algebraic coefficient field generated by \(P\) and \(c\), of the singleton sets \(\{L_c^v(P)\}\) and \(\{U_c^v(P)\}\).  To verify algebraicity, discard every identically zero polynomial from either quantifier-free description.  If no remaining polynomial vanished at its singleton point, all polynomial signs in that description would be constant on a sufficiently small open interval around the point.  The formula would then hold throughout that interval, contradicting that it defines a singleton.  Hence a nonzero polynomial with real algebraic coefficients vanishes at each endpoint, proving that both endpoints are real algebraic.

Finally, lower and upper inclusion are the separate sentences
\[
 \exists z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,L_c^v(P),z_v),
 \qquad
 \exists z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,U_c^v(P),z_v). \tag{5}
\]
Their equivalence to model-side inclusion follows from (1), and they are exactly the tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\).  All coefficients in (5) are algebraic by the preceding paragraph, so elimination and algebraic sign evaluation decide both flags.  This proves the three claims under their separate premises, with no positivity requirement on the cells of \(P\).
